input.text: 'NAGLALARO AKO NG CALL OF DUTY, HINDI KO NAISIP KAILANMAN NA MAMARIL SA LABAS' The rush to blame video games for school violence is not supported by science, a cybersecurity and technology expert said Saturday, pushing back against calls to ban video games in the wake of a shooting incident involving a minor in Tacloban City. Cybersecurity and technology expert Art Samaniego Jr. made the argument in an interview on DZRH News program "Special on Saturday" on July 4, citing research by the Oxford Internet Institute showing no direct link between violent video games and real-world crime or violence. "Naglalaro ako ng Call of Duty, hindi ko naisip kailanman na mamaril sa labas. Maraming pag-aaral ang ginawa na nagpapatunay na walang matibay na ebidensya na nagsasabing ang video game ay may direktang dahilan sa school violence o crime in real life," Samaniego said. He said the real cause of the Tacloban school shooting was not GoreBox—the game the 14-year-old shooter allegedly played—but the people the child was communicating with online, and that extremist recruiters and online predators follow children across platforms regardless of which game or app they use. "Ang tunay na dahilan nun hindi 'yung laro, kundi 'yung mga taong nakakausap nung bata online. Ang dapat nating gawin hindi i-ban 'yung game, kundi tingnan ang kabuuang isyu," Samaniego said. He warned that banning GoreBox specifically is futile since more than 20 similar games exist on mobile platforms alone, and more on PC and console—and children, he said, have no loyalty to specific platforms and will simply migrate to the next available option. Samaniego said the real enforcement gap is not the existence of violent games but the failure to implement existing age ratings—GoreBox is an 18+ game that a 14-year-old was able to access—drawing a direct comparison to the MTRCB film rating system. "Para 'yang sa MTRCB, merong rating. Kung sa MTRCB may ginawang pelikula ang Vivamax tapos may nakapanood na 12-year-old, ipapasara ba natin ang Vivamax? O titingnan natin bakit siya nakapasok sa sinehan dahil mali ang implementation? Ganun lang 'yun dapat ang isipin ng mga lawmakers," Samaniego said.

source_text.preview: 'NAGLALARO AKO NG CALL OF DUTY, HINDI KO NAISIP KAILANMAN NA MAMARIL SA LABAS' The rush to blame video games for school violence is not supported by science, a cybersecurity and technology expert said Saturday, pushing back against calls to ban video games in the wake of a shooting incident involving a minor in Tacloban City. Cybersecurity and technology expert Art Samaniego Jr. made the argument in an interview on DZRH News program "Special on Saturday" on July 4, citing research by the Oxford Internet Institute showing no direct link between violent video games and real-world crime or violence. "Naglalaro ako ng Call of Duty, hindi ko naisip kailanman na mamaril sa labas. Maraming pag-aaral ang ginawa na nagpapatunay na walang matibay na ebidensya na nagsasabing ang video game ay may direktang dahilan sa school violence o crime in real life," Samaniego said. He said the real cause of the Tacloban school shooting was not GoreBox—the game the 14-year-old shooter allegedly played—but the people the child was communicating with online, and that extremist recruiters and online predators follow children across platforms regardless of which game or app they use. "Ang tunay na dahilan nun hindi 'yung laro, kundi 'yung mga taong nakakausap nung bata online. Ang dapat nating gawin hindi i-ban 'yung game, kundi tingnan ang kabuuang isyu," Samaniego said. He warned that banning GoreBox specifically is futile since more than 20 similar games exist on mobile platforms alone, and more on PC and console—and children, he said, have no loyalty to specific platforms and will simply migrate to the next available option. Samaniego said the real enforcement gap is not the existence of violent games but the failure to implement existing age ratings—GoreBox is an 18+ game that a 14-year-old was able to access—drawing a direct comparison to the MTRCB film rating system. output.title: Do video games cause violence? Tacloban shooting triggers debate | ABS-CBN News
output.description: The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are

text.preview: MANILA — The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are being unfairly blamed for a much deeper problem. The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) temporarily blocked access to GoreBox after investigators found that one of the teenage suspects regularly played the game. The June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School left three students dead and 20 others injured, one of the deadliest school shootings in recent Philippine history. But while authorities investigate possible links, experts interviewed on DZMM and ANC warned against drawing a straight line between playing violent games and committing violent crimes. NO EVIDENCE OF LINK Scam Watch Pilipinas co-convenor and cybersecurity journalist Art Samaniego Jr., speaking on DZMM's Balitapatan, pointed to academic research showing no proven causal relationship between violent video games and criminal violence. "May ginawang study kasi sa Oxford Internet Institute, University of Oxford, na wala silang nakita clear link between aggressive behavior sa mga teenager at sa amount of time at kung anong nilalaro nila online." (The Oxford Internet Institute found no clear link between aggressive behavior among teenagers and the amount of time they spend playing online games or the type of games they play.) He went further. "Walang study na nagpapatunay na yung games nakaka-effect sa real life behavior ng gamer. Pero mayroong study nagpapatunay na walang effect ito sa real life behavior nung naglalaro." GoreBox screencap from Google Play (There is no study proving that games affect a gamer's real-life behavior. In fact, there are studies showing they do not affect real-life behavior.) The distinction is crucial because GoreBox itself has more than 10 million downloads worldwide on Google Play and carries a Mature 18+ rating, yet only a tiny fraction of players engage in real-world violence.

output.title: What is GoreBox, the video game linked to one of the Tacloban school shooting suspects?
output.description: The Philippine National Police is now looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in the shooting incident in San Jose National High School in Barangay San Jose, Tacloban City, on Monday may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.

text.preview:
The Philippine National Police is now looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in the shooting incident in San Jose National High School in Barangay San Jose, Tacloban City, on Monday may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.

The shooting incident left three students dead, 15 wounded, and five more with non-firearm-related injuries.

The two suspects, aged 14 and 15, both Grade 9 students and reportedly close friends, allegedly entered two classrooms and opened fire on their schoolmates before they were arrested.

In an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Tuesday, Police Brig. Gen. Jayson Capoy, director of the Police Regional Office in Eastern Visayas, said the 14-year-old suspect had been playing GoreBox.

What is Gorebox?

According to the official Steam page, GoreBox is a physics-driven sandbox game developed by Felix Filip and published by F2 Games.

The game was released on Steam on July 21, 2023, and features a tool called the “Reality Crusher,” which allows players to spawn, manipulate, and destroy objects within the game world.

Known for its graphic depictions of violence, it offers players the opportunity to explore diverse environments and experiment with a variety of weapons, tools, and explosives in a highly interactive sandbox setting.

output.title: Tacloban shooting suspect's violent behavior linked to online game GoreBox
output.description: The Philippine National Police is looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in Monday's fatal shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.
output.text:
The Philippine National Police is looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in Monday's fatal shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.

In an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Tuesday, Police Brig. Gen. Jayson Capoy, director of the Police Regional Office in Eastern Visayas, said the 14-year-old suspect had been playing GoreBox, a sandbox-style game that allows players to create and destroy objects and simulate chaos using various weapons.

Investigators are also looking into reports that the attack may have been rooted in bullying, based on the suspects’ initial statements.

Capoy clarified that the death toll remained at three, while 20 others were injured. Of the injured, 15 sustained gunshot wounds, while the rest were hurt while trying to escape, police said.

The two suspects, aged 14 and 15, both Grade 9 students and reportedly close friends, allegedly entered two classrooms and opened fire on their schoolmates before they were arrested.

Police recovered a Glock pistol and a .38-caliber revolver from the scene. One of the firearms was reportedly issued to a police officer relative, who is now under investigation.

The Department of Education has since coordinated with local authorities and social welfare agencies to provide medical and psychosocial support to affected students and school personnel.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has ordered a full investigation and heightened security measures in schools and other public areas.—MCG GMA News

output.title: FACT CHECK: Hontiveros did NOT call for total ban on online games
output.description: A pro-Leni Robredo Facebook page criticized Sen. Risa Hontiveros for supposedly proposing a ban on online games. This is false and was denied by the senator.

text.preview: Risa Hontiveros proposed a total ban on online games. In a June 30 statement, Sen. Risa Hontiveros denied proposing a “total ban” on any online games, including the controversial violent video game, GoreBox. A pro-Leni Robredo Facebook page criticized Sen. Risa Hontiveros for supposedly proposing a ban on online games following the June 22 school shooting in Tacloban City. This is false, according to the lady senator. The June 29 post has a 153-word caption encouraging the public to hold politicians accountable for their proposals or statements rather than giving them blind loyalty. It featured a graphic with Hontiveros’ photo and the text: “Calling out Risa Hontiveros over her call for a total ban on online games is the right thing to do.” In a June 30 statement, Hontiveros asserted that “[she] never recommended, said, or even thought about banning any game including this GoreBox .” The video game with an R18+ rating “ features extreme violence and graphic depictions of blood and dismemberment” and was reportedly played by one of the teenage shooters prior to the June 22 incident. The senator, who chairs the Senate committee on women, children, family relations and gender equality, began investigating on July 1 the tragic Tacloban City school shooting that left three students dead and 20 others injured. “[W]e hope to examine the broader chain of failures that may have contributed to the June 22 shooting, including possible grooming, radicalization, and normalization of violence in online platforms,” Hontiveros said in a social media post. It was Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla who urged Congress and relevant government agencies to study a potential ban on violent video games, such as GoreBox , in the Philippines. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is open to proposals seeking to ban online games that depict violence amid concerns about their potential influence on the youth, according to Palace Press Officer Claire Castro. output.title: Tacloban shooting may be first 'completed' attack by 764 extremist network — expert
output.description: The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1. Angel Redoble, chair of the Philippine Institute of Cyber Security Professionals, shared his assessment at the Senate panel's first hearing on the June 22 attack at San Jose National High School in Tacloban. The same hearing also saw the Philippine National Police (PNP) disclose that it has rescued at least 24 minors part of the same broad online network since October 2025. Five of the children rescued were found to have harmed themselves. "The first completed mass shooting, if we can finally attribute that to 764, that will be the first," Redoble said. "Because in 2025 [in the United States], it was not completed. It was prevented [and] was foiled." 764 is an extremist network that's been flagged by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation as a "tier one" threat. The group uses blackmail and manipulation to coerce minors into self-harm and explicit acts. It typically operates in decentralized platforms like Discord and Telegram to exploit minors on a global scale. Whether the Tacloban attack is the network's first completed shooting remains unproven, and Redoble and other authorities present at the inquiry stressed repeatedly that the link to 764 was not yet confirmed. Redoble told the committee his earlier research had pointed to groomers of the network mainly based abroad. But that was until foiled attacks in Marikina and Laguna suggested recruiters of 764 were already operating inside the country. When news of the Tacloban shooting broke, he said, his first questions were whether the attackers were gamers and whether the case was tied to 764, both of which, he said, appeared to hold up. output.title: Police link Tacloban campus shooter to violent mobile game
output.description: Police said one of the minors in the Tacloban school shooting had a history of playing a game described as violent.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — One of the minors in the Tacloban City school shooting had a history of playing a game described by police as violent, the Eastern Visayas police said Tuesday, June 23. In a phone interview with reporters, Police Regional Office 8 Director Brig. Gen. Jason Capoy said investigators found that one of the suspects played a game called "Gorebox." "Just like the Roblox, may laro. May shooting, shooting din. May ganoong firearm. Medyo bayolente yung laro," Capoy said. (Just like Roblox, there is a game. There is also shooting. There is that kind of firearm. The game is somewhat violent.) Capoy said the 14-year-old suspect was the one who played the game. According to descriptions on gaming platforms Steam and Google Play, "Gorebox"—which is rated for gamers aged 18 and above—is a "chaotic physics-driven sandbox where creativity meets destruction." Capoy said one of the underage suspects had basic knowledge of firearm handling from a previous visit to a shooting range, including how to release and reload a magazine. Investigators also flagged viral screenshots of text messages allegedly involving the suspects, which Capoy said suggested they had studied the crime and read up on the law. "Napakabilis ng pagkalat ng mga screenshot doon sa text messages nila. Nakakabahala din dahil parang may alam sila. Inaral din nila. Nagbabasa din ng batas," Capoy said. (The screenshots of their text messages spread incredibly fast. It is also alarming because it seems they knew something. They studied it and were also reading the law.) As of 8 a.m. on June 23, the Tacloban City local government, citing the PNP, said 15 people suffered gunshot wounds while five others sustained non-gunshot injuries. Three people were killed in the shooting. Capoy said the aunt of one of the suspects, a police officer, has been placed under restrictive custody . articles.description: The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are

text.preview: MANILA — The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are being unfairly blamed for a much deeper problem. The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) temporarily blocked access to GoreBox after investigators found that one of the teenage suspects regularly played the game. The June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School left three students dead and 20 others injured, one of the deadliest school shootings in recent Philippine history. But while authorities investigate possible links, experts interviewed on DZMM and ANC warned against drawing a straight line between playing violent games and committing violent crimes. NO EVIDENCE OF LINK Scam Watch Pilipinas co-convenor and cybersecurity journalist Art Samaniego Jr., speaking on DZMM's Balitapatan, pointed to academic research showing no proven causal relationship between violent video games and criminal violence. "May ginawang study kasi sa Oxford Internet Institute, University of Oxford, na wala silang nakita clear link between aggressive behavior sa mga teenager at sa amount of time at kung anong nilalaro nila online." (The Oxford Internet Institute found no clear link between aggressive behavior among teenagers and the amount of time they spend playing online games or the type of games they play.) He went further. "Walang study na nagpapatunay na yung games nakaka-effect sa real life behavior ng gamer. Pero mayroong study nagpapatunay na walang effect ito sa real life behavior nung naglalaro." GoreBox screencap from Google Play (There is no study proving that games affect a gamer's real-life behavior. In fact, there are studies showing they do not affect real-life behavior.) The distinction is crucial because GoreBox itself has more than 10 million downloads worldwide on Google Play and carries a Mature 18+ rating, yet only a tiny fraction of players engage in real-world violence.

articles.title: Do video games cause violence? Tacloban shooting triggers debate | ABS-CBN News
articles.description: The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are

text.preview: MANILA — The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are being unfairly blamed for a much deeper problem. The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) temporarily blocked access to GoreBox after investigators found that one of the teenage suspects regularly played the game. The June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School left three students dead and 20 others injured, one of the deadliest school shootings in recent Philippine history. But while authorities investigate possible links, experts interviewed on DZMM and ANC warned against drawing a straight line between playing violent games and committing violent crimes. NO EVIDENCE OF LINK Scam Watch Pilipinas co-convenor and cybersecurity journalist Art Samaniego Jr., speaking on DZMM's Balitapatan, pointed to academic research showing no proven causal relationship between violent video games and criminal violence. "May ginawang study kasi sa Oxford Internet Institute, University of Oxford, na wala silang nakita clear link between aggressive behavior sa mga teenager at sa amount of time at kung anong nilalaro nila online." (The Oxford Internet Institute found no clear link between aggressive behavior among teenagers and the amount of time they spend playing online games or the type of games they play.) He went further. "Walang study na nagpapatunay na yung games nakaka-effect sa real life behavior ng gamer. Pero mayroong study nagpapatunay na walang effect ito sa real life behavior nung naglalaro." GoreBox screencap from Google Play (There is no study proving that games affect a gamer's real-life behavior. In fact, there are studies showing they do not affect real-life behavior.) The distinction is crucial because GoreBox itself has more than 10 million downloads worldwide on Google Play and carries a Mature 18+ rating, yet only a tiny fraction of players engage in real-world violence.

articles.text:
The Philippine National Police is looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in Monday's fatal shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.

In an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Tuesday, Police Brig. Gen. Jayson Capoy, director of the Police Regional Office in Eastern Visayas, said the 14-year-old suspect had been playing GoreBox, a sandbox-style game that allows players to create and destroy objects and simulate chaos using various weapons.

Investigators are also looking into reports that the attack may have been rooted in bullying, based on the suspects’ initial statements.

Capoy clarified that the death toll remained at three, while 20 others were injured. Of the injured, 15 sustained gunshot wounds, while the rest were hurt while trying to escape, police said.

The two suspects, aged 14 and 15, both Grade 9 students and reportedly close friends, allegedly entered two classrooms and opened fire on their schoolmates before they were arrested.

Police recovered a Glock pistol and a .38-caliber revolver from the scene. One of the firearms was reportedly issued to a police officer relative, who is now under investigation.

The Department of Education has since coordinated with local authorities and social welfare agencies to provide medical and psychosocial support to affected students and school personnel.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has ordered a full investigation and heightened security measures in schools and other public areas.—MCG GMA News

articles.text:

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1. Angel Redoble, chair of the Philippine Institute of Cyber Security Professionals, shared his assessment at the Senate panel's first hearing on the June 22 attack at San Jose National High School in Tacloban. The same hearing also saw the Philippine National Police (PNP) disclose that it has rescued at least 24 minors part of the same broad online network since October 2025. Five of the children rescued were found to have harmed themselves. "The first completed mass shooting, if we can finally attribute that to 764, that will be the first," Redoble said. "Because in 2025 [in the United States], it was not completed. It was prevented [and] was foiled." 764 is an extremist network that's been flagged by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation as a "tier one" threat. The group uses blackmail and manipulation to coerce minors into self-harm and explicit acts. It typically operates in decentralized platforms like Discord and Telegram to exploit minors on a global scale. Whether the Tacloban attack is the network's first completed shooting remains unproven, and Redoble and other authorities present at the inquiry stressed repeatedly that the link to 764 was not yet confirmed. Redoble told the committee his earlier research had pointed to groomers of the network mainly based abroad. But that was until foiled attacks in Marikina and Laguna suggested recruiters of 764 were already operating inside the country. The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) temporarily blocked access to GoreBox after investigators found that one of the teenage suspects regularly played the game. The June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School left three students dead and 20 others injured, one of the deadliest school shootings in recent Philippine history. But while authorities investigate possible links, experts interviewed on DZMM and ANC warned against drawing a straight line between playing violent games and committing violent crimes. NO EVIDENCE OF LINK Scam Watch Pilipinas co-convenor and cybersecurity journalist Art Samaniego Jr., speaking on DZMM's Balitapatan, pointed to academic research showing no proven causal relationship between violent video games and criminal violence. "May ginawang study kasi sa Oxford Internet Institute, University of Oxford, na wala silang nakita clear link between aggressive behavior sa mga teenager at sa amount of time at kung anong nilalaro nila online." (The Oxford Internet Institute found no clear link between aggressive behavior among teenagers and the amount of time they spend playing online games or the type of games they play.) He went further. "Walang study na nagpapatunay na yung games nakaka-effect sa real life behavior ng gamer. Pero mayroong study nagpapatunay na walang effect ito sa real life behavior nung naglalaro." GoreBox screencap from Google Play (There is no study proving that games affect a gamer's real-life behavior. In fact, there are studies showing they do not affect real-life behavior.) The distinction is crucial because GoreBox itself has more than 10 million downloads worldwide on Google Play and carries a Mature 18+ rating, yet only a tiny fraction of players engage in real-world violence.

article.description: The Philippine National Police is now looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in the shooting incident in San Jose National High School in Barangay San Jose, Tacloban City, on Monday may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.

text.preview:
The Philippine National Police is now looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in the shooting incident in San Jose National High School in Barangay San Jose, Tacloban City, on Monday may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.

The shooting incident left three students dead, 15 wounded, and five more with non-firearm-related injuries.

The two suspects, aged 14 and 15, both Grade 9 students and reportedly close friends, allegedly entered two classrooms and opened fire on their schoolmates before they were arrested.

In an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Tuesday, Police Brig. Gen. Jayson Capoy, director of the Police Regional Office in Eastern Visayas, said the 14-year-old suspect had been playing GoreBox.

What is Gorebox?

The game was released on Steam on July 21, 2023, and features a tool called the “Reality Crusher,” which allows players to spawn, manipulate, and destroy objects within the game world.

Known for its graphic depictions of violence, it offers players the opportunity to explore diverse environments and experiment with a variety of weapons, tools, and explosives in a highly interactive sandbox setting.

article.title: Tacloban shooting suspect's violent behavior linked to online game GoreBox
article.description: The Philippine National Police is looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in Monday's fatal shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.
article.text:
The Philippine National Police is looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in Monday's fatal shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.

In an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Tuesday, Police Brig. Gen. Jayson Capoy, director of the Police Regional Office in Eastern Visayas, said the 14-year-old suspect had been playing GoreBox, a sandbox-style game that allows players to create and destroy objects and simulate chaos using various weapons.

Investigators are also looking into reports that the attack may have been rooted in bullying, based on the suspects’ initial statements.

Capoy clarified that the death toll remained at three, while 20 others were injured. Of the injured, 15 sustained gunshot wounds, while the rest were hurt while trying to escape, police said.

The two suspects, aged 14 and 15, both Grade 9 students and reportedly close friends, allegedly entered two classrooms and opened fire on their schoolmates before they were arrested.

Police recovered a Glock pistol and a .38-caliber revolver from the scene. One of the firearms was reportedly issued to a police officer relative, who is now under investigation.

The Department of Education has since coordinated with local authorities and social welfare agencies to provide medical and psychosocial support to affected students and school personnel.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has ordered a full investigation and heightened security measures in schools and other public areas.—MCG GMA News

article.title: Tacloban shooting may be first 'completed' attack by 764 extremist network — expert
article.description: The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1. Angel Redoble, chair of the Philippine Institute of Cyber Security Professionals, shared his assessment at the Senate panel's first hearing on the June 22 attack at San Jose National High School in Tacloban. The same hearing also saw the Philippine National Police (PNP) disclose that it has rescued at least 24 minors part of the same broad online network since October 2025. Five of the children rescued were found to have harmed themselves. "The first completed mass shooting, if we can finally attribute that to 764, that will be the first," Redoble said. "Because in 2025 [in the United States], it was not completed. It was prevented [and] was foiled." 764 is an extremist network that's been flagged by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation as a "tier one" threat. The group uses blackmail and manipulation to coerce minors into self-harm and explicit acts. It typically operates in decentralized platforms like Discord and Telegram to exploit minors on a global scale. Whether the Tacloban attack is the network's first completed shooting remains unproven, and Redoble and other authorities present at the inquiry stressed repeatedly that the link to 764 was not yet confirmed. Redoble told the committee his earlier research had pointed to groomers of the network mainly based abroad. But that was until foiled attacks in Marikina and Laguna suggested recruiters of 764 were already operating inside the country. When news of the Tacloban shooting broke, he said, his first questions were whether the attackers were gamers and whether the case was tied to 764, both of which, he said, appeared to hold up. article.title: Police link Tacloban campus shooter to violent mobile game
article.description: Police said one of the minors in the Tacloban school shooting had a history of playing a game described as violent.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — One of the minors in the Tacloban City school shooting had a history of playing a game described by police as violent, the Eastern Visayas police said Tuesday, June 23. In a phone interview with reporters, Police Regional Office 8 Director Brig. Gen. Jason Capoy said investigators found that one of the suspects played a game called "Gorebox." "Just like the Roblox, may laro. May shooting, shooting din. May ganoong firearm. Medyo bayolente yung laro," Capoy said. (Just like Roblox, there is a game. There is also shooting. There is that kind of firearm. The game is somewhat violent.) Capoy said the 14-year-old suspect was the one who played the game. According to descriptions on gaming platforms Steam and Google Play, "Gorebox"—which is rated for gamers aged 18 and above—is a "chaotic physics-driven sandbox where creativity meets destruction." Capoy said one of the underage suspects had basic knowledge of firearm handling from a previous visit to a shooting range, including how to release and reload a magazine. Investigators also flagged viral screenshots of text messages allegedly involving the suspects, which Capoy said suggested they had studied the crime and read up on the law. "Napakabilis ng pagkalat ng mga screenshot doon sa text messages nila. Nakakabahala din dahil parang may alam sila. Inaral din nila. Nagbabasa din ng batas," Capoy said. (The screenshots of their text messages spread incredibly fast. It is also alarming because it seems they knew something. They studied it and were also reading the law.) As of 8 a.m. on June 23, the Tacloban City local government, citing the PNP, said 15 people suffered gunshot wounds while five others sustained non-gunshot injuries. Three people were killed in the shooting. Capoy said the aunt of one of the suspects, a police officer, has been placed under restrictive custody . article.title: FACT CHECK: Hontiveros did NOT call for total ban on online games
article.description: A pro-Leni Robredo Facebook page criticized Sen. Risa Hontiveros for supposedly proposing a ban on online games. This is false and was denied by the senator.

text.preview: Risa Hontiveros proposed a total ban on online games. In a June 30 statement, Sen. Risa Hontiveros denied proposing a “total ban” on any online games, including the controversial violent video game, GoreBox. A pro-Leni Robredo Facebook page criticized Sen. Risa Hontiveros for supposedly proposing a ban on online games following the June 22 school shooting in Tacloban City. This is false, according to the lady senator. The June 29 post has a 153-word caption encouraging the public to hold politicians accountable for their proposals or statements rather than giving them blind loyalty. It featured a graphic with Hontiveros’ photo and the text: “Calling out Risa Hontiveros over her call for a total ban on online games is the right thing to do.” In a June 30 statement, Hontiveros asserted that “[she] never recommended, said, or even thought about banning any game including this GoreBox .” The video game with an R18+ rating “ features extreme violence and graphic depictions of blood and dismemberment” and was reportedly played by one of the teenage shooters prior to the June 22 incident. The senator, who chairs the Senate committee on women, children, family relations and gender equality, began investigating on July 1 the tragic Tacloban City school shooting that left three students dead and 20 others injured. “[W]e hope to examine the broader chain of failures that may have contributed to the June 22 shooting, including possible grooming, radicalization, and normalization of violence in online platforms,” Hontiveros said in a social media post. It was Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla who urged Congress and relevant government agencies to study a potential ban on violent video games, such as GoreBox , in the Philippines. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is open to proposals seeking to ban online games that depict violence amid concerns about their potential influence on the youth, according to Palace Press Officer Claire Castro. text.preview:
The Philippine National Police is now looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in the shooting incident in San Jose National High School in Barangay San Jose, Tacloban City, on Monday may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.

article.title: Tacloban shooting suspect's violent behavior linked to online game GoreBox
article.description: The Philippine National Police is looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in Monday's fatal shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.
article.text:
The Philippine National Police is looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in Monday's fatal shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.

In an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Tuesday, Police Brig. Gen. Jayson Capoy, director of the Police Regional Office in Eastern Visayas, said the 14-year-old suspect had been playing GoreBox, a sandbox-style game that allows players to create and destroy objects and simulate chaos using various weapons.

Investigators are also looking into reports that the attack may have been rooted in bullying, based on the suspects’ initial statements.

Capoy clarified that the death toll remained at three, while 20 others were injured. Of the injured, 15 sustained gunshot wounds, while the rest were hurt while trying to escape, police said.

The two suspects, aged 14 and 15, both Grade 9 students and reportedly close friends, allegedly entered two classrooms and opened fire on their schoolmates before they were arrested.

Police recovered a Glock pistol and a .38-caliber revolver from the scene. One of the firearms was reportedly issued to a police officer relative, who is now under investigation.

The Department of Education has since coordinated with local authorities and social welfare agencies to provide medical and psychosocial support to affected students and school personnel.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has ordered a full investigation and heightened security measures in schools and other public areas.—MCG GMA News

article.title: Tacloban shooting may be first 'completed' attack by 764 extremist network — expert
article.description: The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1. Angel Redoble, chair of the Philippine Institute of Cyber Security Professionals, shared his assessment at the Senate panel's first hearing on the June 22 attack at San Jose National High School in Tacloban. The same hearing also saw the Philippine National Police (PNP) disclose that it has rescued at least 24 minors part of the same broad online network since October 2025. Five of the children rescued were found to have harmed themselves. "The first completed mass shooting, if we can finally attribute that to 764, that will be the first," Redoble said. "Because in 2025 [in the United States], it was not completed. It was prevented [and] was foiled." 764 is an extremist network that's been flagged by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation as a "tier one" threat. The group uses blackmail and manipulation to coerce minors into self-harm and explicit acts. It typically operates in decentralized platforms like Discord and Telegram to exploit minors on a global scale. Whether the Tacloban attack is the network's first completed shooting remains unproven, and Redoble and other authorities present at the inquiry stressed repeatedly that the link to 764 was not yet confirmed. Redoble told the committee his earlier research had pointed to groomers of the network mainly based abroad. But that was until foiled attacks in Marikina and Laguna suggested recruiters of 764 were already operating inside the country. When news of the Tacloban shooting broke, he said, his first questions were whether the attackers were gamers and whether the case was tied to 764, both of which, he said, appeared to hold up. article.title: Police link Tacloban campus shooter to violent mobile game
article.description: Police said one of the minors in the Tacloban school shooting had a history of playing a game described as violent.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — One of the minors in the Tacloban City school shooting had a history of playing a game described by police as violent, the Eastern Visayas police said Tuesday, June 23. In a phone interview with reporters, Police Regional Office 8 Director Brig. Gen. Jason Capoy said investigators found that one of the suspects played a game called "Gorebox." "Just like the Roblox, may laro. May shooting, shooting din. May ganoong firearm. Medyo bayolente yung laro," Capoy said. (Just like Roblox, there is a game. There is also shooting. There is that kind of firearm. The game is somewhat violent.) Capoy said the 14-year-old suspect was the one who played the game. According to descriptions on gaming platforms Steam and Google Play, "Gorebox"—which is rated for gamers aged 18 and above—is a "chaotic physics-driven sandbox where creativity meets destruction." Capoy said one of the underage suspects had basic knowledge of firearm handling from a previous visit to a shooting range, including how to release and reload a magazine. Investigators also flagged viral screenshots of text messages allegedly involving the suspects, which Capoy said suggested they had studied the crime and read up on the law. "Napakabilis ng pagkalat ng mga screenshot doon sa text messages nila. Nakakabahala din dahil parang may alam sila. Inaral din nila. Nagbabasa din ng batas," Capoy said. (The screenshots of their text messages spread incredibly fast. It is also alarming because it seems they knew something. They studied it and were also reading the law.) As of 8 a.m. on June 23, the Tacloban City local government, citing the PNP, said 15 people suffered gunshot wounds while five others sustained non-gunshot injuries. Three people were killed in the shooting. Capoy said the aunt of one of the suspects, a police officer, has been placed under restrictive custody . text.preview: MANILA — The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are being unfairly blamed for a much deeper problem. The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) temporarily blocked access to GoreBox after investigators found that one of the teenage suspects regularly played the game. The June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School left three students dead and 20 others injured, one of the deadliest school shootings in recent Philippine history. But while authorities investigate possible links, experts interviewed on DZMM and ANC warned against drawing a straight line between playing violent games and committing violent crimes. NO EVIDENCE OF LINK Scam Watch Pilipinas co-convenor and cybersecurity journalist Art Samaniego Jr., speaking on DZMM's Balitapatan, pointed to academic research showing no proven causal relationship between violent video games and criminal violence. "May ginawang study kasi sa Oxford Internet Institute, University of Oxford, na wala silang nakita clear link between aggressive behavior sa mga teenager at sa amount of time at kung anong nilalaro nila online." (The Oxford Internet Institute found no clear link between aggressive behavior among teenagers and the amount of time they spend playing online games or the type of games they play.) He went further. "Walang study na nagpapatunay na yung games nakaka-effect sa real life behavior ng gamer. Pero mayroong study nagpapatunay na walang effect ito sa real life behavior nung naglalaro." GoreBox screencap from Google Play (There is no study proving that games affect a gamer's real-life behavior. In fact, there are studies showing they do not affect real-life behavior.) The distinction is crucial because GoreBox itself has more than 10 million downloads worldwide on Google Play and carries a Mature 18+ rating, yet only a tiny fraction of players engage in real-world violence.

articles.title: Tacloban shooting suspect's violent behavior linked to online game GoreBox
articles.description: The Philippine National Police is looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in Monday's fatal shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.
articles.text:
The Philippine National Police is looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in Monday's fatal shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.

In an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Tuesday, Police Brig. Gen. Jayson Capoy, director of the Police Regional Office in Eastern Visayas, said the 14-year-old suspect had been playing GoreBox, a sandbox-style game that allows players to create and destroy objects and simulate chaos using various weapons.

Investigators are also looking into reports that the attack may have been rooted in bullying, based on the suspects’ initial statements.

Capoy clarified that the death toll remained at three, while 20 others were injured. Of the injured, 15 sustained gunshot wounds, while the rest were hurt while trying to escape, police said.

The two suspects, aged 14 and 15, both Grade 9 students and reportedly close friends, allegedly entered two classrooms and opened fire on their schoolmates before they were arrested.

Police recovered a Glock pistol and a .38-caliber revolver from the scene. One of the firearms was reportedly issued to a police officer relative, who is now under investigation.

The Department of Education has since coordinated with local authorities and social welfare agencies to provide medical and psychosocial support to affected students and school personnel.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has ordered a full investigation and heightened security measures in schools and other public areas.—MCG GMA News

articles.description: The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1. Angel Redoble, chair of the Philippine Institute of Cyber Security Professionals, shared his assessment at the Senate panel's first hearing on the June 22 attack at San Jose National High School in Tacloban. The same hearing also saw the Philippine National Police (PNP) disclose that it has rescued at least 24 minors part of the same broad online network since October 2025. Five of the children rescued were found to have harmed themselves. "The first completed mass shooting, if we can finally attribute that to 764, that will be the first," Redoble said. "Because in 2025 [in the United States], it was not completed. It was prevented [and] was foiled." 764 is an extremist network that's been flagged by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation as a "tier one" threat. The group uses blackmail and manipulation to coerce minors into self-harm and explicit acts. It typically operates in decentralized platforms like Discord and Telegram to exploit minors on a global scale. Whether the Tacloban attack is the network's first completed shooting remains unproven, and Redoble and other authorities present at the inquiry stressed repeatedly that the link to 764 was not yet confirmed. Redoble told the committee his earlier research had pointed to groomers of the network mainly based abroad. But that was until foiled attacks in Marikina and Laguna suggested recruiters of 764 were already operating inside the country. When news of the Tacloban shooting broke, he said, his first questions were whether the attackers were gamers and whether the case was tied to 764, both of which, he said, appeared to hold up. text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — One of the minors in the Tacloban City school shooting had a history of playing a game described by police as violent, the Eastern Visayas police said Tuesday, June 23. In a phone interview with reporters, Police Regional Office 8 Director Brig. Gen. Jason Capoy said investigators found that one of the suspects played a game called "Gorebox." "Just like the Roblox, may laro. May shooting, shooting din. May ganoong firearm. Medyo bayolente yung laro," Capoy said. (Just like Roblox, there is a game. There is also shooting. There is that kind of firearm. The game is somewhat violent.) Capoy said the 14-year-old suspect was the one who played the game. According to descriptions on gaming platforms Steam and Google Play, "Gorebox"—which is rated for gamers aged 18 and above—is a "chaotic physics-driven sandbox where creativity meets destruction." Capoy said one of the underage suspects had basic knowledge of firearm handling from a previous visit to a shooting range, including how to release and reload a magazine. Investigators also flagged viral screenshots of text messages allegedly involving the suspects, which Capoy said suggested they had studied the crime and read up on the law. "Napakabilis ng pagkalat ng mga screenshot doon sa text messages nila. Nakakabahala din dahil parang may alam sila. Inaral din nila. Nagbabasa din ng batas," Capoy said. (The screenshots of their text messages spread incredibly fast. It is also alarming because it seems they knew something. They studied it and were also reading the law.) As of 8 a.m. on June 23, the Tacloban City local government, citing the PNP, said 15 people suffered gunshot wounds while five others sustained non-gunshot injuries. Three people were killed in the shooting. Capoy said the aunt of one of the suspects, a police officer, has been placed under restrictive custody . articles.description: The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are

text.preview: MANILA — The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are being unfairly blamed for a much deeper problem. The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) temporarily blocked access to GoreBox after investigators found that one of the teenage suspects regularly played the game. The June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School left three students dead and 20 others injured, one of the deadliest school shootings in recent Philippine history. But while authorities investigate possible links, experts interviewed on DZMM and ANC warned against drawing a straight line between playing violent games and committing violent crimes. NO EVIDENCE OF LINK Scam Watch Pilipinas co-convenor and cybersecurity journalist Art Samaniego Jr., speaking on DZMM's Balitapatan, pointed to academic research showing no proven causal relationship between violent video games and criminal violence. "May ginawang study kasi sa Oxford Internet Institute, University of Oxford, na wala silang nakita clear link between aggressive behavior sa mga teenager at sa amount of time at kung anong nilalaro nila online." (The Oxford Internet Institute found no clear link between aggressive behavior among teenagers and the amount of time they spend playing online games or the type of games they play.) He went further. "Walang study na nagpapatunay na yung games nakaka-effect sa real life behavior ng gamer. Pero mayroong study nagpapatunay na walang effect ito sa real life behavior nung naglalaro." GoreBox screencap from Google Play (There is no study proving that games affect a gamer's real-life behavior. In fact, there are studies showing they do not affect real-life behavior.) The distinction is crucial because GoreBox itself has more than 10 million downloads worldwide on Google Play and carries a Mature 18+ rating, yet only a tiny fraction of players engage in real-world violence.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Hontiveros did NOT call for total ban on online games
articles.description: A pro-Leni Robredo Facebook page criticized Sen. Risa Hontiveros for supposedly proposing a ban on online games. This is false and was denied by the senator.

text.preview: Risa Hontiveros proposed a total ban on online games. In a June 30 statement, Sen. Risa Hontiveros denied proposing a “total ban” on any online games, including the controversial violent video game, GoreBox. A pro-Leni Robredo Facebook page criticized Sen. Risa Hontiveros for supposedly proposing a ban on online games following the June 22 school shooting in Tacloban City. This is false, according to the lady senator. The June 29 post has a 153-word caption encouraging the public to hold politicians accountable for their proposals or statements rather than giving them blind loyalty. It featured a graphic with Hontiveros’ photo and the text: “Calling out Risa Hontiveros over her call for a total ban on online games is the right thing to do.” In a June 30 statement, Hontiveros asserted that “[she] never recommended, said, or even thought about banning any game including this GoreBox .” The video game with an R18+ rating “ features extreme violence and graphic depictions of blood and dismemberment” and was reportedly played by one of the teenage shooters prior to the June 22 incident. The senator, who chairs the Senate committee on women, children, family relations and gender equality, began investigating on July 1 the tragic Tacloban City school shooting that left three students dead and 20 others injured. “[W]e hope to examine the broader chain of failures that may have contributed to the June 22 shooting, including possible grooming, radicalization, and normalization of violence in online platforms,” Hontiveros said in a social media post. articles.title: Do video games cause violence? Tacloban shooting triggers debate | ABS-CBN News
articles.description: The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are

text.preview: MANILA — The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are being unfairly blamed for a much deeper problem. The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) temporarily blocked access to GoreBox after investigators found that one of the teenage suspects regularly played the game. The June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School left three students dead and 20 others injured, one of the deadliest school shootings in recent Philippine history. But while authorities investigate possible links, experts interviewed on DZMM and ANC warned against drawing a straight line between playing violent games and committing violent crimes. NO EVIDENCE OF LINK Scam Watch Pilipinas co-convenor and cybersecurity journalist Art Samaniego Jr., speaking on DZMM's Balitapatan, pointed to academic research showing no proven causal relationship between violent video games and criminal violence. "May ginawang study kasi sa Oxford Internet Institute, University of Oxford, na wala silang nakita clear link between aggressive behavior sa mga teenager at sa amount of time at kung anong nilalaro nila online." (The Oxford Internet Institute found no clear link between aggressive behavior among teenagers and the amount of time they spend playing online games or the type of games they play.) He went further. "Walang study na nagpapatunay na yung games nakaka-effect sa real life behavior ng gamer. Pero mayroong study nagpapatunay na walang effect ito sa real life behavior nung naglalaro." GoreBox screencap from Google Play (There is no study proving that games affect a gamer's real-life behavior. In fact, there are studies showing they do not affect real-life behavior.) The distinction is crucial because GoreBox itself has more than 10 million downloads worldwide on Google Play and carries a Mature 18+ rating, yet only a tiny fraction of players engage in real-world violence.

articles.title: Tacloban shooting suspect's violent behavior linked to online game GoreBox
articles.description: The Philippine National Police is looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in Monday's fatal shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.
articles.text:
The Philippine National Police is looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in Monday's fatal shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.

In an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Tuesday, Police Brig. Gen. Jayson Capoy, director of the Police Regional Office in Eastern Visayas, said the 14-year-old suspect had been playing GoreBox, a sandbox-style game that allows players to create and destroy objects and simulate chaos using various weapons.

Investigators are also looking into reports that the attack may have been rooted in bullying, based on the suspects’ initial statements.

Capoy clarified that the death toll remained at three, while 20 others were injured. Of the injured, 15 sustained gunshot wounds, while the rest were hurt while trying to escape, police said.

The two suspects, aged 14 and 15, both Grade 9 students and reportedly close friends, allegedly entered two classrooms and opened fire on their schoolmates before they were arrested.

Police recovered a Glock pistol and a .38-caliber revolver from the scene. One of the firearms was reportedly issued to a police officer relative, who is now under investigation.

The Department of Education has since coordinated with local authorities and social welfare agencies to provide medical and psychosocial support to affected students and school personnel.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has ordered a full investigation and heightened security measures in schools and other public areas.—MCG GMA News

articles.title: Tacloban shooting may be first 'completed' attack by 764 extremist network — expert
articles.description: The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1. Angel Redoble, chair of the Philippine Institute of Cyber Security Professionals, shared his assessment at the Senate panel's first hearing on the June 22 attack at San Jose National High School in Tacloban. The same hearing also saw the Philippine National Police (PNP) disclose that it has rescued at least 24 minors part of the same broad online network since October 2025. Five of the children rescued were found to have harmed themselves. "The first completed mass shooting, if we can finally attribute that to 764, that will be the first," Redoble said. "Because in 2025 [in the United States], it was not completed. It was prevented [and] was foiled." 764 is an extremist network that's been flagged by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation as a "tier one" threat. The group uses blackmail and manipulation to coerce minors into self-harm and explicit acts. It typically operates in decentralized platforms like Discord and Telegram to exploit minors on a global scale. Whether the Tacloban attack is the network's first completed shooting remains unproven, and Redoble and other authorities present at the inquiry stressed repeatedly that the link to 764 was not yet confirmed. Redoble told the committee his earlier research had pointed to groomers of the network mainly based abroad. But that was until foiled attacks in Marikina and Laguna suggested recruiters of 764 were already operating inside the country. When news of the Tacloban shooting broke, he said, his first questions were whether the attackers were gamers and whether the case was tied to 764, both of which, he said, appeared to hold up. articles.title: Police link Tacloban campus shooter to violent mobile game
articles.description: Police said one of the minors in the Tacloban school shooting had a history of playing a game described as violent.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — One of the minors in the Tacloban City school shooting had a history of playing a game described by police as violent, the Eastern Visayas police said Tuesday, June 23. In a phone interview with reporters, Police Regional Office 8 Director Brig. Gen. Jason Capoy said investigators found that one of the suspects played a game called "Gorebox." "Just like the Roblox, may laro. May shooting, shooting din. May ganoong firearm. Medyo bayolente yung laro," Capoy said. (Just like Roblox, there is a game. There is also shooting. There is that kind of firearm. The game is somewhat violent.) Capoy said the 14-year-old suspect was the one who played the game. According to descriptions on gaming platforms Steam and Google Play, "Gorebox"—which is rated for gamers aged 18 and above—is a "chaotic physics-driven sandbox where creativity meets destruction." Capoy said one of the underage suspects had basic knowledge of firearm handling from a previous visit to a shooting range, including how to release and reload a magazine. Investigators also flagged viral screenshots of text messages allegedly involving the suspects, which Capoy said suggested they had studied the crime and read up on the law. "Napakabilis ng pagkalat ng mga screenshot doon sa text messages nila. Nakakabahala din dahil parang may alam sila. Inaral din nila. Nagbabasa din ng batas," Capoy said. (The screenshots of their text messages spread incredibly fast. It is also alarming because it seems they knew something. They studied it and were also reading the law.) As of 8 a.m. on June 23, the Tacloban City local government, citing the PNP, said 15 people suffered gunshot wounds while five others sustained non-gunshot injuries. Three people were killed in the shooting. Capoy said the aunt of one of the suspects, a police officer, has been placed under restrictive custody . article.title: Do video games cause violence? Tacloban shooting triggers debate | ABS-CBN News
article.description: The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are

text.preview: MANILA — The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are being unfairly blamed for a much deeper problem. The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) temporarily blocked access to GoreBox after investigators found that one of the teenage suspects regularly played the game. The June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School left three students dead and 20 others injured, one of the deadliest school shootings in recent Philippine history. But while authorities investigate possible links, experts interviewed on DZMM and ANC warned against drawing a straight line between playing violent games and committing violent crimes. NO EVIDENCE OF LINK Scam Watch Pilipinas co-convenor and cybersecurity journalist Art Samaniego Jr., speaking on DZMM's Balitapatan, pointed to academic research showing no proven causal relationship between violent video games and criminal violence. "May ginawang study kasi sa Oxford Internet Institute, University of Oxford, na wala silang nakita clear link between aggressive behavior sa mga teenager at sa amount of time at kung anong nilalaro nila online." (The Oxford Internet Institute found no clear link between aggressive behavior among teenagers and the amount of time they spend playing online games or the type of games they play.) He went further. "Walang study na nagpapatunay na yung games nakaka-effect sa real life behavior ng gamer. Pero mayroong study nagpapatunay na walang effect ito sa real life behavior nung naglalaro." GoreBox screencap from Google Play (There is no study proving that games affect a gamer's real-life behavior. In fact, there are studies showing they do not affect real-life behavior.) The distinction is crucial because GoreBox itself has more than 10 million downloads worldwide on Google Play and carries a Mature 18+ rating, yet only a tiny fraction of players engage in real-world violence.

Police recovered a Glock pistol and a .38-caliber revolver from the scene. One of the firearms was reportedly issued to a police officer relative, who is now under investigation.

The Department of Education has since coordinated with local authorities and social welfare agencies to provide medical and psychosocial support to affected students and school personnel.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has ordered a full investigation and heightened security measures in schools and other public areas.—MCG GMA News

article.title: Tacloban shooting may be first 'completed' attack by 764 extremist network — expert
article.description: The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1. Angel Redoble, chair of the Philippine Institute of Cyber Security Professionals, shared his assessment at the Senate panel's first hearing on the June 22 attack at San Jose National High School in Tacloban. The same hearing also saw the Philippine National Police (PNP) disclose that it has rescued at least 24 minors part of the same broad online network since October 2025. Five of the children rescued were found to have harmed themselves. "The first completed mass shooting, if we can finally attribute that to 764, that will be the first," Redoble said. "Because in 2025 [in the United States], it was not completed. It was prevented [and] was foiled." 764 is an extremist network that's been flagged by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation as a "tier one" threat. The group uses blackmail and manipulation to coerce minors into self-harm and explicit acts. It typically operates in decentralized platforms like Discord and Telegram to exploit minors on a global scale. Whether the Tacloban attack is the network's first completed shooting remains unproven, and Redoble and other authorities present at the inquiry stressed repeatedly that the link to 764 was not yet confirmed. Redoble told the committee his earlier research had pointed to groomers of the network mainly based abroad. But that was until foiled attacks in Marikina and Laguna suggested recruiters of 764 were already operating inside the country. When news of the Tacloban shooting broke, he said, his first questions were whether the attackers were gamers and whether the case was tied to 764, both of which, he said, appeared to hold up. text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — One of the minors in the Tacloban City school shooting had a history of playing a game described by police as violent, the Eastern Visayas police said Tuesday, June 23. In a phone interview with reporters, Police Regional Office 8 Director Brig. Gen. Jason Capoy said investigators found that one of the suspects played a game called "Gorebox." "Just like the Roblox, may laro. May shooting, shooting din. May ganoong firearm. Medyo bayolente yung laro," Capoy said. (Just like Roblox, there is a game. There is also shooting. There is that kind of firearm. The game is somewhat violent.) Capoy said the 14-year-old suspect was the one who played the game. According to descriptions on gaming platforms Steam and Google Play, "Gorebox"—which is rated for gamers aged 18 and above—is a "chaotic physics-driven sandbox where creativity meets destruction." Capoy said one of the underage suspects had basic knowledge of firearm handling from a previous visit to a shooting range, including how to release and reload a magazine. Investigators also flagged viral screenshots of text messages allegedly involving the suspects, which Capoy said suggested they had studied the crime and read up on the law. "Napakabilis ng pagkalat ng mga screenshot doon sa text messages nila. Nakakabahala din dahil parang may alam sila. Inaral din nila. Nagbabasa din ng batas," Capoy said. (The screenshots of their text messages spread incredibly fast. It is also alarming because it seems they knew something. They studied it and were also reading the law.) As of 8 a.m. on June 23, the Tacloban City local government, citing the PNP, said 15 people suffered gunshot wounds while five others sustained non-gunshot injuries. article.title: Do video games cause violence? Tacloban shooting triggers debate | ABS-CBN News
article.description: The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are

text.preview: MANILA — The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are being unfairly blamed for a much deeper problem. The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) temporarily blocked access to GoreBox after investigators found that one of the teenage suspects regularly played the game. The June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School left three students dead and 20 others injured, one of the deadliest school shootings in recent Philippine history. But while authorities investigate possible links, experts interviewed on DZMM and ANC warned against drawing a straight line between playing violent games and committing violent crimes. NO EVIDENCE OF LINK Scam Watch Pilipinas co-convenor and cybersecurity journalist Art Samaniego Jr., speaking on DZMM's Balitapatan, pointed to academic research showing no proven causal relationship between violent video games and criminal violence. "May ginawang study kasi sa Oxford Internet Institute, University of Oxford, na wala silang nakita clear link between aggressive behavior sa mga teenager at sa amount of time at kung anong nilalaro nila online." (The Oxford Internet Institute found no clear link between aggressive behavior among teenagers and the amount of time they spend playing online games or the type of games they play.) He went further. "Walang study na nagpapatunay na yung games nakaka-effect sa real life behavior ng gamer. Pero mayroong study nagpapatunay na walang effect ito sa real life behavior nung naglalaro." GoreBox screencap from Google Play (There is no study proving that games affect a gamer's real-life behavior. In fact, there are studies showing they do not affect real-life behavior.) The distinction is crucial because GoreBox itself has more than 10 million downloads worldwide on Google Play and carries a Mature 18+ rating, yet only a tiny fraction of players engage in real-world violence.

text.preview:
The Philippine National Police is now looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in the shooting incident in San Jose National High School in Barangay San Jose, Tacloban City, on Monday may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.

article.title: Tacloban shooting suspect's violent behavior linked to online game GoreBox
article.description: The Philippine National Police is looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in Monday's fatal shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.
article.text:
The Philippine National Police is looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in Monday's fatal shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.

In an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Tuesday, Police Brig. Gen. Jayson Capoy, director of the Police Regional Office in Eastern Visayas, said the 14-year-old suspect had been playing GoreBox, a sandbox-style game that allows players to create and destroy objects and simulate chaos using various weapons.

Investigators are also looking into reports that the attack may have been rooted in bullying, based on the suspects’ initial statements.

Capoy clarified that the death toll remained at three, while 20 others were injured. Of the injured, 15 sustained gunshot wounds, while the rest were hurt while trying to escape, police said.

The two suspects, aged 14 and 15, both Grade 9 students and reportedly close friends, allegedly entered two classrooms and opened fire on their schoolmates before they were arrested.

Police recovered a Glock pistol and a .38-caliber revolver from the scene. One of the firearms was reportedly issued to a police officer relative, who is now under investigation.

The Department of Education has since coordinated with local authorities and social welfare agencies to provide medical and psychosocial support to affected students and school personnel.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has ordered a full investigation and heightened security measures in schools and other public areas.—MCG GMA News

article.title: Tacloban shooting may be first 'completed' attack by 764 extremist network — expert
article.description: The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1. Angel Redoble, chair of the Philippine Institute of Cyber Security Professionals, shared his assessment at the Senate panel's first hearing on the June 22 attack at San Jose National High School in Tacloban. The same hearing also saw the Philippine National Police (PNP) disclose that it has rescued at least 24 minors part of the same broad online network since October 2025. Five of the children rescued were found to have harmed themselves. "The first completed mass shooting, if we can finally attribute that to 764, that will be the first," Redoble said. "Because in 2025 [in the United States], it was not completed. It was prevented [and] was foiled." 764 is an extremist network that's been flagged by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation as a "tier one" threat. The group uses blackmail and manipulation to coerce minors into self-harm and explicit acts. It typically operates in decentralized platforms like Discord and Telegram to exploit minors on a global scale. Whether the Tacloban attack is the network's first completed shooting remains unproven, and Redoble and other authorities present at the inquiry stressed repeatedly that the link to 764 was not yet confirmed. Redoble told the committee his earlier research had pointed to groomers of the network mainly based abroad. But that was until foiled attacks in Marikina and Laguna suggested recruiters of 764 were already operating inside the country. When news of the Tacloban shooting broke, he said, his first questions were whether the attackers were gamers and whether the case was tied to 764, both of which, he said, appeared to hold up. article.title: Police link Tacloban campus shooter to violent mobile game
article.description: Police said one of the minors in the Tacloban school shooting had a history of playing a game described as violent.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — One of the minors in the Tacloban City school shooting had a history of playing a game described by police as violent, the Eastern Visayas police said Tuesday, June 23. In a phone interview with reporters, Police Regional Office 8 Director Brig. Gen. Jason Capoy said investigators found that one of the suspects played a game called "Gorebox." "Just like the Roblox, may laro. May shooting, shooting din. May ganoong firearm. Medyo bayolente yung laro," Capoy said. (Just like Roblox, there is a game. There is also shooting. There is that kind of firearm. The game is somewhat violent.) Capoy said the 14-year-old suspect was the one who played the game. According to descriptions on gaming platforms Steam and Google Play, "Gorebox"—which is rated for gamers aged 18 and above—is a "chaotic physics-driven sandbox where creativity meets destruction." Capoy said one of the underage suspects had basic knowledge of firearm handling from a previous visit to a shooting range, including how to release and reload a magazine. Investigators also flagged viral screenshots of text messages allegedly involving the suspects, which Capoy said suggested they had studied the crime and read up on the law. "Napakabilis ng pagkalat ng mga screenshot doon sa text messages nila. Nakakabahala din dahil parang may alam sila. Inaral din nila. Nagbabasa din ng batas," Capoy said. (The screenshots of their text messages spread incredibly fast. It is also alarming because it seems they knew something. They studied it and were also reading the law.) As of 8 a.m. on June 23, the Tacloban City local government, citing the PNP, said 15 people suffered gunshot wounds while five others sustained non-gunshot injuries. Three people were killed in the shooting. Capoy said the aunt of one of the suspects, a police officer, has been placed under restrictive custody .
